companies.latest_signal: Core Local Commerce swung back to +RMB5.7bn profit (7.9% margin) in Q2 2026 from a -RMB2bn Q1 loss; per Tencent News coverage, management said instant-delivery unit economics turned positive 'ahead of schedule' but cautioned industry subsidy levels 'remain elevated compared to 2024,' with CEO Wang Xing crediting March 2026 regulatory pressure for pushing the industry from subsidy-burning toward service competition.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: Alibaba China E-Commerce Group Adjusted EBITA YoY decline
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba discloses no standalone instant-commerce loss figure; the closest proxy is the YoY decline in Adjusted EBITA of the 'Alibaba China E-Commerce Group' segment (Taobao+Tmall+Ele.me+Fliggy), which management explicitly attributes to Taobao Instant Commerce/quick-commerce investment
companies.latest_signal: FY27 Q1 (quarter ended June 2026) filing states Taobao Instant Commerce 'continued to improve its unit economics quarter-over-quarter while maintaining market share'; the EBITA YoY drag essentially closed (-1% vs -76% a year earlier), and 21jingji/36kr coverage (Aug 2026) describes all three players as having moved past the 'hot-war' phase of the subsidy fight.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_name: New Businesses segment loss from operations
companies.metric_basis: JD does not break out food delivery losses standalone; the disclosed proxy is operating loss of the 'New Businesses' reportable segment, which bundles JD Food Delivery/JD Takeaway with Dada, Jingxi and Joybuy
companies.latest_signal: CFO Ian Su Shan said New Businesses losses 'narrowed significantly year-on-year, primarily driven by continued loss reduction at JD Food Delivery'; Sina Finance's Aug 2026 management Q&A quantified total JD Food Delivery investment as down more than 50% YoY, attributed to efficiency gains and order-mix shift toward full-meal orders rather than subsidy cuts alone.

war_summary: Subsidy intensity peaked in Q3 2025 across all three combatants (Meituan Core Local Commerce -RMB14.1bn, Alibaba's China E-Commerce EBITA -76% YoY, JD New Businesses -RMB15.7bn), coinciding with the most aggressive instant-retail/food-delivery price war; a March 2026 regulatory 'anti-involution' push (cited explicitly by Meituan's Wang Xing) accelerated a shift from cash subsidies toward service/order-economics competition. By Q2 2026 all three show clear sequential and YoY narrowing — Meituan is back to segment profit first, Alibaba's EBITA drag is nearly eliminated, and JD's New Businesses loss has nearly halved from its peak — though management across all three still caveats that subsidy levels remain above the pre-war 2024 baseline and full normalization is still several quarters out.
